original_study.citation: Connors AF Jr et al. The effectiveness of right heart catheterization in the initial care of critically ill patients. JAMA. 1996;276(11):889–897.

permission.basis: Repository permission to use datasets; cite original paper and acknowledge Vanderbilt. No separate named CC/ODC licence was stated on the page inspected.
permission.required_acknowledgement: Data obtained from http://hbiostat.org/data courtesy of the Vanderbilt University Department of Biostatistics.

transformations_to_source: None. Retained original bytes, unnamed row index, NA markers, leading spaces, all patients and source fields.

teaching_encoding.x: 0=Female, 1=Male, using released sex field; this is the source categorisation, not a claim about gender identity.
teaching_encoding.a: 0=No RHC, 1=RHC in first 24 hours after study entry (swang1).
teaching_encoding.y: 0=No, 1=Yes from released dth30 (30-day mortality from study entry).
teaching_encoding.exclusions: None from released 5735-row cohort. Original SUPPORT eligibility restrictions remain.
teaching_encoding.estimand: Early hand calculations: sex-standardised observed-data mortality risk difference (Psi_X). Lesson 8: W-standardised observed-data mortality risk difference (Psi_W), using the same 5735 patients. Causal interpretation of either requires additional unverified assumptions.

w.design_definition: Intercept, male indicator, standardised age, race_black and race_other indicators, and 12 history/comorbidity fields. Q additionally includes A.

audit.date_origin_evidence: Official rhc.sav sadmdte/dthdte origin attribute: month=1, day=1, year=1960; numerical values agree with CSV. Downloaded separately for metadata verification; not an analysis input.

design_limits: RHC was observationally selected even though SUPPORT phase II randomised a different decision-support intervention.
Original cohort excluded death or discharge within 48 hours; do not generalise to all newly eligible ICU patients or claim a clean baseline target-trial emulation.
Treatment is classified over first 24 hours; no exact catheter insertion time is released.
Day-1 physiology uses worst value in a 24-hour window, so pre-RHC ordering is not established.
Original study confirms date of death or survival to day180 for all patients; last contact field alone is not a death censoring date.
Sex alone cannot control confounding by indication; adding all day-1 measurements is not automatically valid baseline adjustment.
